newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Caribbean countries eye expanded trade with Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean countries eye expanded trade with Cuba.

text.p: A trade agency representing 15 Caribbean countries said Tuesday it opened an office in Havana and began scouting for opportunities for exporters interested in the region's largest market.

Richard Wells, a Jamaican named to head the Barbados-based Caribbean Export Development Agency's new office, said in an interview in Kingston he was convinced that Cuba's burgeoning tourism market provided an opening for Caribbean companies to export everything from building materials to food and drinks.
"Cuba's industry can't meet this sector's needs over the short to medium term," Wells said.

He said Cuba expected to gross $1 billion from a million visitors this year, and planned to build 3,000 rooms every year to accommodate the 2.5 million to 3.5 million visitors expected by the end of the decade, Wells stated

No accurate figures exist on current trade levels between Cuba and other countries in the Caribbean region. Estimates range from between $30 million and $100 million a year, most of it coming in the form of petroleum products from Trinidad.

Wells said some businesses have shied away from Cuba recently out of concern about the Helms-Burton Act, an U.S. law that seeks to apply an American embargo against Cuba to foreign companies with business interests in the island nation.
"I'm hoping to be able to erode that perception," Wells said. "Caribbean exporters are not really affected by the law, and those without assets in the U.S. are pretty safe."

He said the absence of competition from the United States provided Caribbean exporters with an extra edge to establish a market presence, so "once the embargo is lifted, we can still retain some market share."
The office was opened at the request of the Cuban authorities, who signaled about two years ago that they wanted other countries in the region to open a trade outpost in Cuba.
"I can't think of any other government that is as willing to accomodate Caribbean exporters as the Cubans are," Wells said.

The four-year-old Caribbean Export Development Agency was created with funding from the European Union and the governemnts of members of the Caribbean Community (Caricom), an economic alliance of English-speaking Caribbean nations, the Dominican Republic and Haiti.
